name: Pochoir plate
summary: A plate coloured by hand through a set of stencils, each one for a colour, in gouache and watercolour on a printed key line. Iribe and Lepape made the Poiret albums in 1908 and 1911; Barbier and the Gazette du Bon Ton made it the look of Art Deco fashion.

philosophy.core_thesis: A stencil and a brush give a flat, opaque and luminous colour that no press can match.
design_principles: Print a thin key line in black or grey, then put each colour on by hand through its own stencil.
Use 4–30 flat, opaque colours of gouache, with gold and silver for accents.
Keep each colour area flat and clean, with a soft edge where the brush meets the stencil.
Use a slim, elongated figure in a simple pose against a large area of bare paper.
Let one bright colour (a rose, a jade, a lacquer red) carry the plate.
Add a decorative pattern only in the dress or the background, never in both.
anti_patterns: A halftone dot or a gradient
Thick, dark outlines like a comic
A full-colour background that leaves no bare paper

process.matrix: A set of stencils cut from zinc, copper or celluloid, one for each colour, and a printed key line.
process.press: No press for the colour: a pochoiriste uses a round brush (pompon) through each stencil.
process.image_making: The artist paints the original; the atelier (Saudé) cuts the stencils and colours each sheet by hand.
process.edition: Some hundreds to a few thousand copies for a magazine or an album.

inks.strategy: Gouache and watercolour, mixed by eye for each colour, with metallic powders for gold and silver.

screening.rule: Put each colour on flat and opaque; there is no screen and no overprint mix.

registration.rule: Each stencil aligns by eye to the key line; a small gap or overlap shows the hand.

substrate.stock: A heavy, smooth wove paper (Arches or vellum paper) that holds gouache without cockling.
substrate.finish: Smooth wove, uncoated, bright white to cream.

surface.impression: No bite; the gouache sits on the paper as a thin, chalky film.
surface.sheen: Matt, velvet colour, with gold that catches the light.
surface.texture: Flat colour with a soft brush edge and slight unevenness inside each area.

marks: small gaps at the key line

positive: theatre, ballet and myth in evening dress

emotion.target_response: Elegance and luxury: the viewer feels a refined, modern taste of the 1920s.

avoid_when: The image needs realistic tone or a photograph.
The budget forbids a flat, simple drawing style.

modifiers.how: Change the hand stencils for riso drums in 2–3 bright inks with a transparent overprint.
Add a frame of chevrons, sunbursts and stepped forms in gold.

sources.title: Jean Saudé, Traité d'enluminure d'art au pochoir (1925)
